questions.q: What problem did ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION solve, starting in SQL Server 2016?
options: It let query-processing settings like MAXDOP be tuned per database instead of only at the server level
It introduced the transaction log for the first time
It replaced ALTER DATABASE entirely
It only applies to tempdb
questions.explain: Before 2016, settings like max degree of parallelism were server-wide; database-scoped configuration lets each database carry its own override without affecting others on the instance.

questions.q: What does the database-scoped MAXDOP setting override?
options: The server-level max degree of parallelism, but only for that one database
The recovery model of the database
The collation of the database
The file growth settings of the database
questions.explain: A database-scoped MAXDOP lets one database (say, a reporting workload) run with different parallelism than another database on the same instance.

options: Whether the database uses the modern (2014+) or legacy pre-2014 cardinality estimator
Whether AUTO_SHRINK is enabled
Whether the database is read-only
The database's recovery model
questions.explain: This setting toggles between cardinality estimator models per database — useful when an upgrade changes plan shapes for the worse and reverting buys time to tune properly.

questions.q: What does setting PARAMETER_SNIFFING = OFF change?
options: The optimizer stops caching a plan based on the first parameter value it saw for a query
It disables all query optimization
It forces every query to recompile on every execution regardless of parameters
It turns off statistics collection entirely
questions.explain: Turning off parameter sniffing stops the optimizer from basing a cached plan on the first-seen parameter value — useful when that causes bad-plan reuse, at the cost of losing sniffing's benefit elsewhere.

questions.q: What does the FOR SECONDARY clause allow in database-scoped configuration?
options: A readable secondary replica in an Availability Group can have different settings than the primary
It duplicates the primary database's files onto a second disk
It only applies to tempdb secondary files
It disables database-scoped configuration on secondaries
questions.explain: FOR SECONDARY lets a readable AG secondary — which might serve a different workload like reporting — carry its own database-scoped settings distinct from the primary.
